lens: Still-image hierarchy, reading comfort, discoverability of story and whole-world coherence across supplied scales.
evidenceMethod: All listed images viewed. Full-width originals were displayed by the tool at 2048 pixels; native crops preserve local detail. Supplied 1280/880/420 images are image scales only.

score.scope: Whole still-image craft within Interaction B’s hierarchy and comfort lens; not animation or interface quality.

deductions.finding: Uneven material finish after the later pass
deductions.location: 11 native hero face/antennae and bench, tree bark and workshop wood; compare 07 native crops.
deductions.effect: The more conspicuous cellular/crackle-like lines spread across cream, green and wooden surfaces. They make unlike materials feel processed alike, draw attention to surface noise and weaken the soft coherent film-world finish. This is visible at native size and in the 1280 image, not only at 5x.

deductions.finding: Dense detail competes with secondary story clarity
deductions.location: Left tree/root grass, workshop tabletop/toolbox and bright path at 880/420.
deductions.effect: Characters remain separated, but flowers, wood edges and lighting flecks compete with the small building/play actions. At 420 the leaf activity and hammer grip become incidental marks. This is a small-size tradeoff, not a demand that every cameo be recognizable.

deductions.finding: Posed rather than absorbed coding beat
deductions.location: Foreground face and gaze above the laptop.
deductions.effect: The reader-facing smile is welcoming and the keyboard contact conveys coding, but the gaze gives the hero a promotional-pose quality rather than fully absorbed activity. This is a modest artistic deduction, not a factual anatomy defect.

criteriaForNine: Keep the present composition, cast count, warm directional light and coder dominance while restoring quieter, materially distinct face/wood/foliage surfaces at native and 1280 size.
Preserve the clear 420-pixel hero silhouette and 880-pixel secondary grouping without adding labels or enlarging the guests.
Keep the three activities readable as optional layers of the same calm world; any adjusted gaze or gesture must retain the tiny innocent identity and grounded keyboard/bench contact.
Any revised export must retain the corrected flat Grok eyes and dark Muse eyes when inspected at native and magnified scale. No unseen revision earns nine automatically.

strengths: The whole environment participates in the direction: canopy framing, curved path, workshop shelter, bench, pond and bridge form a credible layered park rather than pasted character cutouts.
The large bright cream head, glasses and laptop anchor the right foreground at all three supplied scales. The four guests stay small and left; they do not defeat the coder’s hierarchy.
Warm upper-right light, rim highlights, grounded bench/stools and softer distant bridge create spatial continuity. The knitting, books and cup support a quiet working atmosphere.
The left resting cluster and central workshop reward closer inspection without making their discovery necessary to read a warm coding scene.
Grok’s two white ovals are visibly pupil-free in the enlarged crop; Muse retains dark eyes. No current eye blocker found.

mustFix.priority: before calling the whole scene finished
mustFix.location: Native hero crop, especially cream forehead/cheek and bench slats; corresponding tree/workshop surfaces.
mustFix.issue: The later version’s conspicuous crackle/cellular surface treatment reduces the material separation and soft finish achieved in 07.
mustFix.requestedOutcome: A restrained local material cleanup or controlled return toward the cleaner 07 rendering, preserving 11’s intentional story and eye corrections. Avoid a fresh whole-frame restyle that alters already working hierarchy.
mustFix.verification: Compare final and 07 native hero/workshop crops plus final 1280 view; the improvement must be visible without requiring magnification.

optional: Consider slightly quieter high-frequency foliage/wood detail around the workshop and root play group; preserve world richness and leave character scale unchanged.

A slightly more laptop-directed gaze could make the coding beat feel less posed, but the current smile and keyboard contact already communicate a welcoming coder. This does not block presentation by itself.
baselineComparison: 07 and 11 share the strong composition, warm park lighting, foreground exclusivity and four guests. 11’s Grok eyes are larger clean flat ovals and its workshop moth is compact. 07’s hero face, bench and workshop wood read smoother and more materially differentiated. I prefer 11’s explicit eye correction but 07’s quieter finish; neither fact warrants replacing the complete scene blindly.

skillsReviewed.application: Judge actual rendered hierarchy and details, and avoid polishing one small feature while degrading the complete picture.
Inspect the same scene at large, medium and small supplied scales, plus native and magnified crops; separate scale tradeoffs from defects.

skillsReviewed.reading: Previously read in full; reused selectively
skillsReviewed.application: Maintain evidence boundaries: a 420-pixel image is not a phone test.

skillsReviewed.reading: Previously read full main SKILL; reused selectively
skillsReviewed.application: Ground the judgment in coherent material/hierarchy and actual images rather than a style label.

skillsReviewed.reading: Previously read in full; scope exception only
skillsReviewed.application: This static picture supplies no timing, cadence or input behavior to assess.

workflowChanges: Compare whole frame and supplied scales before eye close-ups so local corrections cannot pre-approve global finish.
For every future targeted raster edit, compare unchanged hero/material regions against the accepted baseline before declaring the correction complete.
Keep named visible defects, optional artistic preferences and unobserved audience interpretation separate.
rulesNotApplicableWithReason: UI timing, focus, touch-target, hover, scrolling and compositor recipes do not apply to this static-image review.
Commercial full-screen layouts, custom fonts and page animation recipes cannot improve the image’s material finish.
Optional background cameos need not remain individually identifiable at 420 pixels; mandatory recognition would be a different brief.
limits: No browser, actual GitHub placement, physical device, display-calibration or screen-reader test was performed.
No animation, sound, interactive scene, website behavior, human attention or return-visit response is scored.
The intended three appearances of one moth and parent/kids metaphor remain authorial readings; these images do not establish unprimed audience interpretation.
Observed texture differences are real visual comparisons; their production cause is not established.
This is an independent still-image recommendation, not full-team approval or approval of replacement art.
